s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion and associated skin changes
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral, affecting the right thigh and buttock
Recent limitation of motion in the right limb joint
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings included normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Alcian blue staining was negative

shortlist.label: Stiff skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening and limited joint motion

shortlist.label: Segmental stiff skin syndrome (SSS)
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the segmental distribution of skin hardening and associated skin changes

shortlist.label: Linear Scleroderma (Morphea)
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the unilateral skin involvement and joint limitation

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of skin thickening and limited joint motion

shortlist.label: Morphea profunda
shortlist.why_kept: A subtype of morphea that could explain the deep tissue involvement and skin changes

raw.rationale: The patient's unilateral skin hardening, recent limitation of motion in the right limb joint, and histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts with normal epidermis are consistent with Segmental stiff skin syndrome (SSS). The condition's progressive nature over 7 years and the absence of systemic inflammation or autoantibodies also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Stiff skin syndrome
rejected.why: Stiff skin syndrome typically presents with more widespread and symmetrical skin involvement, which is not consistent with the patient's unilateral presentation.

rejected.label: Linear Scleroderma (Morphea)
rejected.why: Linear Scleroderma (Morphea) often presents with more distinct, linear bands of sclerosis and may involve deeper tissues, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of a large, ill-defined plaque with mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic fasciitis is characterized by acute onset, rapid progression, and significant eosinophilia, which is not consistent with the patient's 7-year history of progressive skin hardening and normal laboratory results.

rejected.label: Morphea profunda
rejected.why: Morphea profunda is a subtype of localized scleroderma that involves deeper tissues, including the subcutis and fascia, and often presents with more pronounced sclerosis and atrophy, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of mild skin changes and lack of significant inflammation or atrophy.
